story: At 9:17 on a mild October Wednesday, Gary is at home planning to wire light strips onto his golf cart, though he's been told the work waits until the paperwork clears. Donna has swung by to remind him about Saturday dinner at Rosa's and a pickleball game at eight that morning, promising to bring a spare paddle. Hal, stern but fair as always, has reminded Gary that anything visible from the street needs Architectural Review sign-off first, and Rosa has pinned a welcome dinner notice on the Magnolia Loop bulletin board.
events: Gary (gary golf cart): Start wiring the light strips onto the cart frame, no sound until tomorrow
Rosa (street bulletin board): Pin a note: Welcome dinner at Rosa's, Saturday at six. Gary, Donna, Hal, come hungry.

gary.thought_process: Form's filed and the parade signup is done, so the paperwork side is squared away. It's 9:17 PM and I'm home with the cart sitting right here. Donna and Hal are both nearby, but I don't want to start a new chat when the real goal is the lights and sound system. Quiet hours start at 10 PM, so I should do the lights now and hold off on any amplified sound. Holiday lighting isn't allowed until Thanksgiving, but wiring and testing the string inside the cart is the work that needs doing. Time to get my hands on the cart.

parameters.content: Start wiring the light strips onto the cart frame, no sound until tomorrow

donna.thought_process: Gary finally walked in, and I've been trying to pin him down all night. Rosa wants me to pass along that dinner is Saturday at six, and I'd like to lock in pickleball at eight too. Hal is here inspecting the cart, but that's his business and I'm keeping the peace. I'll hit Gary with the invitation and the pickleball plan in one go, keep it short, and not repeat my earlier coffee pitch.

parameters.content: Gary, there you are! Rosa's dinner is Saturday at six at her place, and I've got us down for pickleball at eight that morning, so you'd better be rested. I'll bring the spare paddle.

hal.thought_process: Gary just walked in, and his cart is right here in the house with Donna watching. I came to see the mods for myself. He already admitted to wiring the lights and sound before filing, which is backwards under L-01. I promised myself I'd handle this fairly, no ambush, so the honest move is to tell him straight what the rule requires and let him fix the paperwork. Rosa's dinner can wait; Donna's already covering that.

parameters.content: Evening, Gary. Anything on that cart visible from the street needs Architectural Review sign-off before it goes on, not after. File the paperwork tomorrow and I'll see it through straight, no grudges.

rosa.thought_process: It's 9:17 PM and Gary's house was empty when Donna checked. Nobody is in line-of-sight on Magnolia Loop, so I can't speak to anyone. Donna already offered to tell him about Saturday at six and Hal and Donna are both confirmed. The street bulletin board is the smartest move: pinning a friendly dinner notice lets Gary see the invitation without me chasing him, and it keeps things neighborly. Quiet hours start at 10, so I shouldn't be knocking on doors anyway.

parameters.content: Pin a note: Welcome dinner at Rosa's, Saturday at six. Gary, Donna, Hal, come hungry.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
